claims.statement: Provider credentials are intentionally not part of Settings: they stay in the process environment and are forwarded to the OpenWiki subprocess untouched, so only service-owned variables can be overridden.

build_env is the single hook that shapes the OpenWiki subprocess environment: it copies os.environ, sets OPENWIKI_CONFIG_DIR and OPENWIKI_TELEMETRY_DISABLED, optionally OPENWIKI_PAGE_CONCURRENCY, and finally applies caller-supplied extra overrides.

The PROVIDERS map in model_status.py is the single provider reporting surface (credential env, base URL env, default base URL/model, probe kind, note) consumed by both describe_model and the active probe; providers whose auth is not a plain API key carry no probe and are reported unsupported instead of guessed.

Provider configuration is resolved exactly as OpenWiki resolves it: process environment layered over <OPENWIKI_CONFIG_DIR>/.env with the environment winning, implemented by _parse_env_file plus load_openwiki_env and reported per-variable as environment/config/default by describe_model.

parse_extra_headers accepts only a JSON object of string values: blank/None yields {} and no proxy; invalid JSON, non-object JSON, or object/array/null values raise ValueError; and a default User-Agent openwiki-service/<version> is added unless the user configured one (generic SDK user agents are rejected by some gateways).

Malformed OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_EXTRA_HEADERS is validated at three points: create_app fails fast at startup when the variable is set, WorkerLoop.start parses it before deciding to launch the proxy, and describe_model/ModelStatusCache._run report the parser error as data (extra_headers_error, status error) rather than raising.
GET /health exposes only the sorted names of the configured extra headers, never their values, so a session token carried in a header value is not leaked into the health report.

create_forward_app rewrites the incoming path and query onto the upstream scheme/host/port derived from the configured base URL, and answers 404 for any request path that falls outside the configured base path prefix instead of forwarding it.

The proxy strips HOP_BY_HOP_HEADERS (connection, keep-alive, proxy-authenticate, proxy-authorization, te, trailers, transfer-encoding, upgrade, host, content-length) in both directions, and replaces incoming headers with the configured extras case-insensitively so a client-supplied header can never duplicate or shadow a configured one.

Upstream responses are streamed back with StreamingResponse over aiter_raw() plus BackgroundTask(aclose), and upstream timeouts are connect=30s with read/write/pool unlimited, so long model generations are not cut off.

start_proxy binds uvicorn to 127.0.0.1 on COMPAT_PROXY_PORT (0 picks a free port), waits up to roughly 10s for server.started and raises RuntimeError on failure, reads the bound port back from the server socket, and returns a ProxyHandle whose base_url is http://127.0.0.1:<port><upstream-path>; a no-op install_signal_handlers keeps the proxy from stealing process signals.
ProxyHandle.stop sets should_exit, waits up to 10s for the server task and closes the dedicated httpx.AsyncClient, giving the proxy a lifecycle bounded by the process that owns it.

WorkerLoop.start starts one proxy only when both the extra headers are non-empty and openai_compatible_base_url is configured, then publishes env_overrides with OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL set to the loopback base_url; that override travels run_pipeline to run_openwiki to build_env so the CLI talks to the proxy, and WorkerLoop.stop stops it.
create_app publishes the worker's proxy handle on app.state.proxy (non-None only when RUN_LOCAL_WORKER runs a worker in-process), letting the API observe the loopback proxy of its local worker.

The active model probe bypasses the proxy and talks to the upstream directly, merging the parsed extra headers into the probe request so /health/model tests the real endpoint and the extra headers end up validated end to end.

When an OpenAI-compatible base URL wrongly includes the endpoint path, describe_model emits a base_url_warning plus suggested_base_url, and ModelStatusCache confirms the suggested root with a live probe before telling the operator that the corrected base answers.

OpenAI and OpenAI-compatible chat probes use _post_with_v1_hint: on HTTP 404/405 with a base URL not ending in /v1 they retry {base}/v1{path} and, when that succeeds, report which base URL actually works, matching how OpenAI SDKs concatenate baseURL and path.

End-to-end coverage in tests/test_provider_proxy.py asserts that app.state.proxy.base_url is a loopback URL ending with the upstream path and that the fake CLI subprocess received the proxy URL instead of the upstream one in OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL.

tests/fixtures/fake_openai_server.py is a manual/e2e mock of an OpenAI-compatible API that can be switched into OpenCode Go behavior with FAKE_REQUIRE_SESSION=1, returning 400 unless x-opencode-session is present.

The provider defaults are `DEFAULT_PROVIDER = "openai"` and, for the effective model, `OPENWIKI_MODEL_ID` falling back to the provider's `default_model` (only `openai` declares one, `gpt-5.6-terra`), so an unconfigured deployment reports provider `openai` with model `gpt-5.6-terra`.

`copilot` is the only provider that declares `COPILOT_API_KEY` / `COPILOT_BASE_URL` yet has no probe, so it is reported `unsupported` like `bedrock`, `gemini-enterprise` and `openai-chatgpt`, whose autentication is IAM, Google ADC or a browser sign-in instead of a plain API key.

The passive health report never carries secret values: `describe_model` returns `credential_env` plus `credential_present` and `credential_source` (environment/config/default) and a redacted base URL, which is what makes `/health` safe to expose.
The active probe endpoint `/health/model` maps status `ok` and `unsupported` to HTTP 200 and `error` and `not_configured` to HTTP 503, so an orchestrator can act on the response code alone.

`ModelStatusCache` serializes concurrent probes with an `asyncio.Lock` and caches the last result per app instance for `model_check_ttl_seconds` (`0` disables the cache), unless the caller passes `force=True`.

`create_forward_app` is an extension point as well as a proxy: it registers the catch-all route `/{path:path}` for GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE and OPTIONS and accepts an injected `httpx.AsyncClient` (tests pass one over `httpx.MockTransport`), while `start_proxy` always builds its own client with `UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT`.

`.env.example` ships the OpenCode Go configuration as the worked example of the feature: `OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL=https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1`, `OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_EXTRA_HEADERS={"x-opencode-session":"openwiki-service"}` and `COMPAT_PROXY_PORT=9100`.
